query: Which material can be used for enhance glass-forming ability, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Introducing 5–8 at% palladium (Pd) into a base Zr-based alloy will significantly increase its glass-forming ability compared to the undoped alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: A Zr-based metallic glass alloy, initially free of Pd doping.
generation.intervention: Doping the alloy with 5–8 atomic percent of Pd.
generation.conditions: Prepare the alloy under identical melting and casting conditions (e.g., vacuum induction melting, water-cooled copper mold casting).
generation.structural_mediator: Pd atoms alter the short-to-medium range order of the melt, hindering the nucleation of stable crystalline phases.
generation.mechanism: Pd doping increases the atomic packing frustration, raising the thermodynamic barrier to crystallization and thus enhancing the likelihood of retaining an amorphous structure upon cooling.
generation.predicted_outcome: Critical casting diameter (a common measure of glass-forming ability) will increase by approximately 20% compared to the undoped Zr-based alloy.
generation.baseline: In the undoped alloy, the maximum amorphous casting thickness is lower (e.g., <5 mm) under the same processing conditions.
generation.boundary: Effects may diminish at Pd contents significantly above 8 at%, as excessive additions can lead to secondary phase precipitation, reducing glass-forming ability.
generation.uncertainty: Data on other compositions, cooling rates, or higher Pd additions remain limited.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce both undoped and Pd-doped samples of varying compositions and cast them into cylindrical rods of increasing diameters using identical parameters.
measurements: Confirm amorphous structure with X-ray diffraction (no sharp Bragg peaks).
Measure critical casting diameter at which crystallinity appears.
Perform differential scanning calorimetry to compare crystallization onset temperatures.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Pd-doped samples show no greater critical casting diameter than the undoped control or fail to exhibit higher crystallization onset temperatures, the hypothesis is not supported.
